items.abstract: <jats:p>As the building industry moves toward sustainability and intelligent structures, there&apos;s been an increased demand for integrated energy management solutions that synchronize renewable energy systems, HVAC systems, and smart electrical networks. Studies of these subsystems are often conducted separately, however, and there is limited research investigated in an integrated framework to explain how these subsystems work together in building energy systems. This study reviews the latest advancements in integration of renewable energy, HVAC optimization, and smart electrical network management in buildings, from a structured literature review and a systems-integration approach. Dominant technologies, operational coordination methods, optimization methods, and sustainability aspects of intelligent building energy systems were identified by analyzing relevant peer-reviewed literature. The concept of ML-IBEMF is proposed and introduced in this paper, which aims to integrate renewable energy generation systems, HVAC optimization mechanism, smart electrical coordination and digital intelligence technologies into a unified analytical framework, connecting to sustainability performance outcomes. The research also advances the theory of intelligent buildings, sustainable energy and sustainable building design and offers practical design and management recommendations for those using intelligent building energy systems.</jats:p>

items.abstract:
<jats:p>Dense urban environments are exposed to the combined effects of rising global temperatures and urban heat islands. This combination is resulting in increasing trends of energy consumption in cities, associated mostly with air conditioning to maintain indoor human comfort conditions. During periods of extreme summer weather, electrical usage usually reaches peak loads, stressing the electrical grid. The purpose of this study is to explore the use of available, high resolution weather data by effectively preparing a building for peak load management.</jats:p>
               <jats:p>The subject of study is a 14 floor, 620,782 sq ft building located in uptown Manhattan, New York City (40.819257 N, −73.949288 W). To precisely quantify thermal loads of the buildings for the summer conditions; a single building energy model (SBEM), the US Department of Energy EnergyPlus™ was used. The SBEM was driven by a weather file built from weather data of the urbanized weather forecasting model (uWRF), a high resolution weather model coupled to a building energy model. The SBEM configuration and simulations were calibrated with winter actual gas and electricity data using 2010 as the benchmark year. In order to show the building peak load management, demand response techniques and technologies were implemented. The methods used to prepare the building included generator usage during high peak loads and use of a thermal storage system. An ensemble of cases was analyzed using current practice, use of high resolution weather data, and use of building preparation technologies. Results indicated an average summer peak savings of more than 30% with high resolution weather data.</jats:p>
